transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diego Flores (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Cardinal CTO), Owen Brooks (Cardinal ML Eng), Rita Chen (Cardinal Platform Lead), Samir Rao (Cardinal Security), Speaker 2

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through integration options, discussed SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway vs proxy patterns, concerns around rate limiting and quotas, and observability needs. Customer interested in pilot, wants benchmarks and security docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, I'm Alex from Redwood, i have Priya and Diego with me — thanks for doing this sync. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maya: good afternoon yeah thanks, excited to hear how you all think about integrating with our platform.
[00:12] Owen: quick context — we're a data-driven insights product, lots of short prompts and some long form summarization, latency sensitive for interactive features, also big batch workloads. we've evaluated a bunch of runtimes.
[00:24] Priya: quick question about the stack — are you currently running anything open-source models in prod or using managed hosted providers?
[00:29] Owen: currently hybrid, we run smaller models on prem for embeddings and use a managed provider for generation. but licensing costs and latency are trending up. Also we have a gateway proxy in front of our microservices.
[00:39] Rita: yes we have a central API gateway that handles auth/rate-limits, it's a Kong+Envoy mix, and some teams use a sidecar pattern for model calls.
[00:48] Diego: perfect, that's the kind of detail that helps — Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and fully private VPC/on-prem installs, and our SDKs have first-class integrations for LangChain and LlamaIndex.
[00:58] Maya: can you unpack the SDK story? are there client libraries for node/python and examples for LangChain?
[01:05] Alex: absolutely — we have Python and Node SDKs, plus some SDK helpers that map to LangChain chains and LlamaIndex retriever interfaces. I'll share code snippets, but the short is: you can drop-in a Redwood client and swap in a Redwood LLM wrapper for langchain.llms, or use the Redwood embeddings client in LlamaIndex so the indexing pipeline is seamless.
[01:22] Owen: nice. is there any adapter or connector code you maintain or do we need to glue it ourselves?
[01:28] Priya: we maintain community recipes and some first-party connectors. for common patterns like chains + caching we provide examples. most customers add a small adapter layer for app-specific logic.
[01:36] Rita: important for us — we already use in-house request tracing and want distributed traces down to model calls. how does Redwood emit traces or hooks?
[01:44] Diego: good one — we support opentelemetry traces emitted from the SDK out-of-the-box, and on the server side we provide request IDs, token-level cost breakdowns, and per-request latency metrics that can be exported to prometheus/grafana or to your observability pipeline.
[01:57] Samir: about security — do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM? we can't have keys stored by third-parties for some workloads.
[02:04] Alex: yes, for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and some HSMs). for hosted we offer envelope encryption — keys in Redwood KMS but we can discuss bring-your-own-key for enterprise plans. will include SOC2 docs in the pack.
[02:18] Maya: on deployment modes — we want deterministic latency. how much variance do you see between hosted and dedicated?
[02:24] Priya: hosted is multitenant and optimized for quick time-to-value, typical p95 latency for a standard 4k-token generation is X ms on our profiles, but workloads differ. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and much more predictable p95/p99. for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated or Private. we'll run benchmarks for your prompt shapes to give numbers.
[02:43] Owen: ok, we need to see both cost and latency. one friction is our gateway rate-limits — we apply quotas at the API gateway level. how do Redwood rate limits interact? can you do token quotas or rate per-account?
[02:55] Diego: yes — Redwood supports multi-dimension quotas: requests-per-minute, tokens-per-day, and custom billing units. you can enforce per-project or per-api-key quotas. with a gateway in front you can mirror those limits or let Redwood be rate authoritative and have the gateway enforce local policies — either works.
[03:13] Rita: if we keep the gateway as the front, we'd prefer a sidecar or adapter that forwards headers and correlates request IDs, not rewrite traffic.
[03:21] Priya: sidecar pattern is supported. we also have a proxy-first integration where your gateway forwards to Redwood via secure mTLS and we preserve headers for tracing and auth.
[03:30] Speaker 2: (inaudible) what's the cost impact if we want low latency with small batch sizes?
[03:36] Alex: small batch sizes increase per-token cost — Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching profiles. Dedicated helps because you control concurrency and can set continuous batching thresholds. we'll show cost models that compare hosted bursting vs dedicated steady-state.
[03:52] Maya: do you support KV cache or prefix caching for chat workloads? that's critical for our convo UX.
[03:58] Priya: yes we have KV cache support and prefix caching. with private/dedicated you get more control over cache lifetime and can pin caches to sessions. in hosted we do prefix caching as well but with shared eviction policies that are still high-perf. sometimes the auto-transcribe says KK V cache — forgive the ai — but it's KV.
[04:15] Owen: about open-source model support — can we bring our own model weights into your dedicated/private infra? we may have fine-tuned variants.
[04:23] Diego: Private or Dedicated can run customer model artifacts; for hosted we curate models for performance and safety. for private deployments we provide onboarding docs for model bundle formats and kernel/quantization recommendations.
[04:36] Rita: network topology question — if we want private and keep the control plane managed, how does traffic route, and who stores logs?
[04:43] Alex: in our Private mode we can operate a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or a hybrid model. logs and audit trails can be pushed to your S3 or logging endpoint and we integrate with cloud logging and SIEMs. we'll itemize retention options in the security pack.
[04:58] Samir: what about compliance: can we get a SOC2 attestation and penetration test reports?
[05:03] Alex: yes, SOC2 and penetration reports available for enterprise — will attach. for private deployments we can also support on-site audits if needed.
[05:12] Owen: curious about SDK behavior on transient errors — we use retries with idempotency and need clear guidance on when to retry vs fallback.
[05:20] Priya: SDK implements retryable error semantics and exposes hooks so you can implement circuit breakers and fallback policies. also we support streaming fallback to smaller models if the main model times out.
[05:33] Maya: on observability, you mentioned token-level cost, can we break down cost per route or per customer?
[05:40] Diego: yes — Redwood Console exposes token-level cost per-api-key, per-route, per-model. you can tag requests with business context and get cost reports per-customer. we also emit traces and percentiles.
[05:51] Rita: we have strict SLAs with our customers, so we'd want to define a fallback strategy that doesn't surface poor quality outputs. do you offer canary rollouts and automatic fallback?
[05:59] Alex: yup — rollouts, canaries, A/B are supported. you can pin versions and specify automatic fallback to a cheaper model or a cached response. that capability is in Redwood Console.
[06:10] Owen: let's talk about LangChain and LlamaIndex specifics — LlamaIndex retrievers often expect synchronous embedding calls and chunking; do you have a recommended pattern?
[06:20] Priya: recommended pattern: run embeddings in batches using our embeddings client, store vectors in your existing vector store, and use our SDK hooks for prefetching embeddings for likely candidates. we include code for chunking and canonical examples for LlamaIndex.
[06:32] Owen: are there known gotchas e.g., tokenization differences that break similarity scoring?
[06:37] Diego: tokenization can differ, we note model tokenizer in metadata and we recommend normalizing text pre-indexing. sometimes token counts in our telemetry differ from naive tokenizers — we'll share a small calc script.
[06:50] Maya: on the topic of quotas again — can you throttle at the model level so that a noisy route doesn't starve others?
[06:58] Priya: absolutely — per-route and per-model throttles are supported; you can set priority routing and hard or soft limits. plus you can configure token budgets per-API-key.
[07:09] Samir: encryption at rest and in-transit — we need TLS and customer-managed keys for private data. also audit trail preservation for 7 years is required for some customers.
[07:18] Alex: TLS everywhere, plus we support pushing logs to your archive. for very long retention we can export to your S3 with lifecycle rules; we'll document retention and cost.
[07:27] Rita: integration effort — what's typical for onboarding, code changes, and how long is a pilot?
[07:33] Priya: usually a 3-4 week pilot: week 0-1 gather prompts and traffic patterns and run small benchmarks, week 2 integrate SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, week 3 run canary on a customer subset and evaluate cost/latency. small infra changes if you're using sidecar; otherwise minimal.
[07:48] Owen: do you have example infra templates or helm charts for sidecar or envoy integration?
[07:53] Diego: yes, we'll share helm charts and envoy filters we've used before. also example nginx/istio configs.
[07:59] Speaker 2: (cross talk) question about A/B testing — how do we collect quality metrics to decide which model wins?
[08:05] Alex: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets and you can wire your evaluation metrics in. we can run truth-labeled prompt sets and produce regression alerts.
[08:15] Maya: any stories of customers doing heavy embedding pipelines and cost-saving patterns?
[08:20] Priya: some customers batch embeddings and cache intermediate vectors, use quantized models for cheap vector generation, and schedule large batch runs off-peak. Redwood Optimize suggests when to quantize.
[08:30] Owen: one last technical question — do you support LLM tool-calling or structured outputs? we need deterministic JSON outputs for downstream processing.
[08:38] Diego: yes structured output and function calling is supported; our SDK helps enforce schemas and we return structured payloads with confidence signals.
[08:47] Rita: ok sounds good — let's talk about next steps.
[08:50] Alex: recap: we'll send pricing, SOC2/security pack, SDK snippets, helm/sidecar templates, and run a benchmark on your samples. you'll share sample prompts and traffic. Diego/Priya will run the bench and we reconvene for a private/VPC deep dive.
[09:05] Maya: thanks everyone, that timeline works tentatively.
[09:09] Owen: quick note — we have an internal legal kickoff next Wed, could be a gating item for private deploy.
[09:14] Samir: I'll look at the security pack, may request a follow-up on encryption details.
[09:18] Alex: perfect, we'll target sending materials by Friday.
[09:21] (meeting ends)
